spans.s:
श्नु श्नु, (in grammar) a technical term for
the affix नु, the characteristic sign of the fifth class
of roots.

स्नु 1. स्नु (probably connected with rt.
स्ना), cl. 2. P. स्नौति, सुष्णाव, स्नविष्-
यति, अस्नावीत्, स्नवितुम्, to drip, trickle, distil, fall
in drops, drop, ooze, run out, leak; to flow, stream;
cl. 2. A. (Pass. reflex.) स्नुते, अस्नोष्ट or अस्ना-
विष्ट: Pass. स्नूयते, स्नोता or स्नाविता, स्नोष्-
यते or स्नाविष्यते, Aor. अस्नावि, to be distilled,
&c.: Caus. स्नावयति, &c., Aor. असुष्णवत्:
Desid. of Caus. सिस्नावयिषति or सुस्नावयिषति
[]
(according to Vopa-deva): Desid. सुस्नूषति: In-
tens. सोष्णूयते, सोष्णवीति, सोष्णोति; [cf. Gr.
νέ-ω (for σνεϝ-ω), νεύ-σω (for σνεύ-σω), νεῦ-σι-ς,
νευ-σ-τήρ, νά-ω (for σναϝ-ω), ἀένα-ο-ς, νᾶ-μα,
νᾱ-ρό-ς, νη-ρό-ς, Νη-ρ-εύ-ς, Νη-ιά-(δ)-ς; (probably also
ναῦ-ς, ναύ-τη-ς, &c., see under 3. नौ, p. 518):
Goth. snu, ‘to go;’ sniva, snau, snivum (for snu-
um), snaivs, ‘snow:’ Old Germ. sniutan, sniumi,
sneo, snê: Angl. Sax. sniwan, snytan, sneome:
Lith. snega-s (w being changed to g): Slav. snêg:
Hib. snuadhaim, ‘I flow;’ snuadh, ‘blood;’
sneachd, ‘snow.’]

स्नु 3. स्नु, उस्, f. = स्नायु, a sinew, tendon,
muscle.
—स्नु-तस्, ind. from the sinews or muscles.

स्नु 4. स्नु, a Kṛd-anta affix to roots form-
ing adjectives expressive of an aptitude to be what is
implied by the root; [cf. स्थास्नु.]

स्नुत, अस्, आ, अम्, trickled, distilled, dropped,
trickling, flowing, dropping, oozing.

स्नुति, इस्, f. trickling, distilling, oozing, stream,
flow.
स्नुत्वा, ind. having trickled or oozed or flowed.

स्नुच् स्नुच्, cl. 1. A. स्नोचते, &c., to be
bright or clear (probably for rt. स्तुच्, but
according to Śabda-k., under ष्णुच्, the meaning is
सेचने).

स्नुषा स्नुषा, f. (said to be fr. rt. 1. स्नु),
a daughter-in-law; the milk-hedge plant (= 2. स्नुह्);
[cf. Gr. νυό-ς; Lat. nuru-s (for snusu-s); Old
Germ. snur; Angl. Sax. snoru; Slav. snochâ.]

स्नुस् स्नुस्, cl. 4. P. स्नुस्यति, सुस्नोष,
स्नोसितुम्, to eat; to disappear or become
invisible; to take.

स्नुह् 1. स्नुह्, cl. 4. P. स्नुह्यति, सुष्णोह,
स्नोहितुम् or स्नोग्धुम् or स्नोढुम्, to
vomit; = rt. 1. स्निह्.

2. स्नुह्, ट्, ट्, ट्, or क्, क्, क्, vomiting, one who
vomits; (क्), f. the milk-hedge plant, Euphorbia
Antiquorum (its milky juice has various medicinal pro-
perties, and is used as an emetic; seventeen synonyms
of this plant are enumerated, cf. सीहुण्ड).
—स्नुक्-
छद, अस्, m. a kind of reed (= क्षीर-कञ्चुकिन्).
स्नुहि, इस्, or स्नुही, f. = 2. स्नुह् above.
